slides.headline: THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW *AI could do*
slides.body: Part 3. Five tools that do something you probably assumed was impossible. I am a software developer and I used all five this week.
slides.close: Number 1 is the one *nobody believes until they hear it*.

slides.headline: IT CAN *clone your voice*
slides.body: ElevenLabs takes about a minute of you talking and builds a copy of your voice. Type anything and it says it back, sounding like you.
slides.close: It will also speak languages *you do not speak*.

slides.headline: IT TURNS YOUR NOTES INTO *a podcast*
slides.body: Drop your documents into NotebookLM and hit audio overview. Two hosts show up and discuss your files like a real show.
slides.close: Your own notes, in your ears, *on the drive to work*.

slides.headline: IT WRITES *actual songs*
slides.body: Suno takes one sentence and hands you back a full track. Vocals, instruments, structure, all of it.
slides.close: People are using it for background music and *nobody can tell*.

slides.headline: IT MAKES IMAGES WITH *readable text*
slides.body: Nano Banana Pro renders words you can actually read. Almost every other image model turns text into scrambled letters.
slides.close: Which is why it can make *your covers and your thumbnails*.

slides.headline: IT TURNS A PHOTO INTO *a video*
slides.body: Upload one still to Kling, describe the motion you want, and get moving footage back a minute later.
slides.close: Most of the b roll you scroll past *started as a single image*.

slides.headline: COMMENT *HIDDEN*
slides.body: I will send you all five with the links, plus which ones are free.
slides.close: No email needed. Save this and *send it to someone who thinks AI is just chatbots*.
